findings.title: T12 tells the reader on G2 that every representation of the board 'needs more than the game', which SPEC 2.18 and M8 beat 7 contradict
findings.location: site/src/components/tools/t12/rep.ts:441-444 (noMinusculeSentence, data-out="no-minuscule"); shown on every node of G2 at /tools/rep/
findings.claim: On G2, F4 and E8, T12 prints 'This board has no minuscule node; its representations need more than the game.' For G2 this is false by the specification. SPEC 2.18's other recipe, 'One zero weight', builds the 7-dimensional representation of G2 from the game ([V]). The code cites SPEC 2.18 [D], but that [D] covers only the representations out of reach of both recipes.
findings.expected: SPEC 2.18 'One zero weight': 'the 7-dimensional representation of G2 ... The Chevalley-Serre relations hold [V for A1, B2, B3, B4 and G2]. This gives the site a route to G2 that stays inside the game'. 'Out of reach of these two recipes: every other representation ... says plainly that the matrices need more than the game [D]'. M8 beat 7 on the same lesson: 'the 7-dimensional representation of G2. A later version of this module builds them from single steps as well.' On G2 the sentence should say that the minuscule recipe builds none of its representations, without claiming every representation needs more than the game.
findings.observed: /tools/rep/?z=1&g=G2&k=1 and k=2, hydrated, data-out="no-minuscule": 'This board has no minuscule node; its representations need more than the game.' noMinusculeSentence(buildRepresentation(G2, 1)) returns the same string. Golden orbit_plus_zero_representations[type=G2;highest_weight=1,0].dimension is 7.
findings.reproduction: Clean checkout of 006f50d plus site/tests/unit/redteam-RT-08-p5-g2-sentence.test.ts, then npm ci --prefer-offline && npx vitest run site/tests/unit/redteam-RT-08-p5-g2-sentence.test.ts. Result: 2 failed (G2 node 1 and node 2), 1 passed (golden check). If the stale Vite SSR cache error appears, set TMPDIR to a fresh directory.
findings.specRef: SPEC.md 2.18 'One zero weight' and 'Out of reach' [D]; SPEC 3 M8 beat 7; golden orbit_plus_zero_representations[type=G2]; RED-TEAM-COMMON 4 ('a mathematical statement presented as fact that is wrong')
findings.proposedFix: Scope the sentence to the recipe, for example: 'This board has no minuscule node, so the recipe of this tool builds none of its representations.' On G2 it may add that the one-zero-weight recipe (phase 7) reaches the 7.

findings.title: Attack 13: two M8 <G> paths print the right digits from the wrong record (the string through (2, 0) from the node-2 representation, and the determinant of three boards from E8 alone)
findings.claim: Beat 1 and b1's caption print the middle position (0, 1) of the string through (2, 0) at node 1 of A2 with the path of a weight of another representation, the orbit of the fundamental position of node 2, whose positions do not include (2, 0). Beat 6 says 'E8, F4 and G2 have no minuscule node: their Cartan matrices have determinant <G k="types.E8.det_cartan"/>', so the path names one of the three boards the sentence names. Both print the right digits only by coincidence. The lesson already computes the string with the engine (export const STRING_TWO = stringThrough(A2, [2, 0], 0), never used).
findings.expected: SPEC 7.3: <G> exists 'so prose cannot drift from the data'. The lens rule: a path whose board or field differs from the sentence is a finding even when the digits agree. Expected: (0, 1) from STRING_TWO, or typed (the string has no golden record); the beat 6 determinant from types.E8, types.F4 and types.G2 together, or the sentence limited to E8.
findings.observed: stringThrough(A2, [2, 0], node 1) = [[2,0],[0,1],[-2,2]]. The golden weights of the A2 node-2 representation are [[1,-1],[0,1],[-1,0]]: entry [1] equals (0, 1), but (2, 0) is not in that representation. M8 lines 61 and 65 use that path or fmt(wt('A2', 2, 1)). Line 113 prints the determinant of three boards from types.E8.det_cartan.
findings.reproduction: Clean checkout of 006f50d plus site/tests/unit/redteam-RT-08-p5-wrong-path.test.ts, then npm ci --prefer-offline && npx vitest run site/tests/unit/redteam-RT-08-p5-wrong-path.test.ts. Result: 2 failed (lines 61 and 65; line 113), 1 passed (the coincidence check).

notes: For RT-09: T12's 'Dimension' readout shows the orbit size on nodes that are not minuscule. E8 node 8 shows 'Dimension: 240' while M8 beat 6 and SPEC 2.18 give the representation on the Lie algebra of E8 as 248. F4 node 4 shows 24 against the 26 of F4, and G2 node 1 shows 6 against 7. E8 node 1 shows 'Dimension: 2160' with no matrices built. The P5-A3 review raised this as out of scope, and it was not repaired.

For the owner: 'Gabriel's theorem ... first proved in [Gab72]' (M8 sidebar and the not-quiver page) is a priority claim. Neither SPEC nor SOURCES states it: [Gab72] is 'Citation [S]' only, and SPEC 2.16 names the theorem without a source. It is historically standard, so it is not reported. A sentence in SOURCES 11.3 or an E18 item would settle it.

For RT-09 or the owner: the not-quiver page says Kostant's 'every move raises one city by exactly one Martian, and every population met is a positive root population: both verified by computation for every simply laced board of finite type of rank at most eight'. verify.py section 9 checks one random play from each starting node, not every play. The form-value argument on the same page covers the general case.

M8's Seen-box E10 fallback, 'It is found in the standard texts on Lie algebras.', asserts the content of books SOURCES 11.0 limit 2 says were not opened, the pattern of confirmed P3-RT-08-07. It is not reported because SPEC 2.18 labels the fact 'Standard' and only the section numbers [U]. 'This is a standard fact of Lie theory.' alone would avoid the question.

M8's b5 reveal types the golden list types.D4.minuscule_nodes as 'Nodes 1, 3 and 4 are the minuscule nodes of D4', and b11's explanation types the labels of types.D5.minuscule_nodes. Not reported, because the lens exempts node labels; as="word" exists for such lists.

SOURCES 11.0 limit 1: [W03a]'s 'Theorem 4.1' (M8 Seen) and 'Proposition 3.5' (not-quiver) were read in the preprint, while the [W03a] entry cites the journal version on ScienceDirect. SPEC F2 labels Proposition 3.5 [S], and [Gre07] [S] corroborates Theorem 4.1, so this is not reported.

Glossary gap for the owner: M8 defines string, single step, the Chevalley-Serre relations, signed move and (on the page) quiver in bold, but the glossary has no entries for them. The P5-A3 request to the glossary owner (P1-A4) was not acted on in phase 5.
Positions are spaced inconsistently within one M8 sentence: typed Tex '(2,0)' beside <G> '(0, 1)' (beat 1). Style only.
Word counts: M1 (release, the lessons' own rule) is at exactly 1800 and M3 at 1797, as in phase 4. M8 is at 1795 in the preview and 1797 in the release. No room is left for edits.
